promotion_scope: Capability-gated bounded non-interactive Linux host-process primitive only; interactive PTY, ClayCode string/argv lowering and whole CM-TERM/ClayMachine acceptance remain open.
hypothesis: A shell-free argv process primitive with explicit capability admission, clean environment, bounded dual-pipe capture, timeout and fresh process-group termination can establish the first real CM-TERM control-plane foothold without inventing PTY or ClayCode string semantics.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Dual stdout/stderr pipe pressure can deadlock a superficially bounded wrapper when one pipe fills while the controller waits on the other.

unusual_experiment.name: DUAL_PIPE_70K_NO_NEWLINE
unusual_experiment.input: 70000 A bytes to stdout + 70000 B bytes to stderr, no newline, timeout 2.0 s, combined budget 200000 bytes

overlap_regressions.workflow: ClayCode runtime nominal boundary repair VPS

remaining_blockers: Interactive PTY and live bidirectional stream semantics
Canonical ClayCode byte/string and argv/env/cwd/stdin/stdout/stderr lowering through checker -> executable IR -> single ClayVM -> ClayOS
Broader typed filesystem/process/network/device authority and receipts
next_discriminator: Select the smallest canonical Clay byte/string plus argv value and transport one literal ClayCode argument through executable IR into the single VM, then bind it to linux.process.spawn.v0 without shell semantics.
